Working notes:

- Do not treat claim size, category, or filing channel alone as evidence of fraud. Small online claims (CLM-7001, 7006, 7007) were approved but later found fraudulent, so apply enhanced scrutiny where risk indicators exist rather than automatically approving modest claims.
- Large claims can be valid across home, health, and auto (CLM-7002, 7008, 7009, 7010); amount alone is not grounds for rejection.
- Avoid rejecting solely because supporting documentation is not mentioned or appears incomplete. Several valid claims were rejected and later appealed successfully (CLM-7003, 7005, 7008). Request or verify documentation instead.
- Approve when the reported loss is plausible and normal checks support coverage, incident details, damage/medical necessity, and estimates (CLM-7002, 7004, 7009, 7010).
- Use a conditional/verification-first approach: confirm policy coverage, date and circumstances of loss, claimant consistency, documentation, repair or treatment estimates, and fraud indicators before final approval.
- Online submissions and small payouts may warrant additional fraud screening, but there is no universal channel or amount rule.

Working notes:

- Claim size, category, and channel are not conclusive alone. Large claims across home, health, and auto can be valid; small phone claims can also be valid (CLM-7012).
- A strong recent pattern links small online claims with later-confirmed fraud (CLM-7001, 7006, 7007, 7015–7020; CLM-7011 was correctly rejected). Treat small online submissions as high-risk, requiring enhanced or independent verification before approval. Do not approve merely because the loss is plausible or no fraud indicator is supplied.
- For small online claims, verify policy coverage, incident timing and consistency, medical necessity or physical damage, provider/repair documentation, and authenticity of invoices or records. Escalate, defer, or reject when evidence cannot be independently validated or discrepancies emerge.
- Do not reject solely because documentation is absent from the initial description or appears incomplete. Request and verify it first; valid claims were previously rejected and later upheld on appeal (CLM-7003, 7005, 7008).
- Approve when normal checks substantiate coverage, circumstances, claimant consistency, necessity/damage, and credible estimates or documentation (CLM-7002, 7004, 7009–7014).
- Paper and phone channels are not inherently safe, and large amounts are not grounds for rejection. Use a verification-first approach, with risk-based escalation rather than universal amount or channel rules.

Working notes:

- Claim size, category, and channel are not conclusive alone. Large claims across home, health, and auto can be valid (CLM-7002, 7004, 7009–7014, 7024, 7029–7030); small claims can also be valid (CLM-7012, 7027–7028).
- Small online claims show a strong fraud pattern (CLM-7001, 7006–7007, 7011, 7015–7020, 7022–7023, 7025–7026). Treat them as high-risk and require enhanced or independent verification before approval, but do not reject automatically.
- For any claim, verify coverage, incident timing and consistency, claimant account, necessity or physical damage, provider/repair documentation, estimates, and invoice/record authenticity. Escalate or defer when evidence is insufficient or cannot be independently validated.
- Missing or incomplete information in the initial description is not grounds for rejection. Request the documents and perform checks first; valid claims were wrongly rejected when this was not done (CLM-7003, 7005, 7008, 7021, 7027–7028).
- Approve when normal checks substantiate coverage, circumstances, claimant consistency, necessity/damage, and credible documentation. A large amount or paper/phone submission is not itself suspicious or grounds for rejection.
- Use verification-first, risk-based decisions: approve supported claims, request evidence or escalate uncertain ones, and reject only when fraud, ineligibility, or material contradictions are established.

Working notes:

- Size, category, and channel are not conclusive alone. Large claims across health, auto, and home can be valid (CLM-7002, 7004, 7009–7014, 7024, 7029–7031, 7036); small claims can also be valid (CLM-7012, 7027–7028, 7032, 7035, 7038, 7040). Paper and phone submissions are not inherently suspicious.
- Small online claims show a strong fraud pattern (CLM-7001, 7006–7007, 7011, 7015–7020, 7022–7023, 7025–7026, 7034, 7037, 7039). Treat them as high-risk and require enhanced, independent validation, but do not reject solely from channel or amount.
- For every claim, verify coverage and eligibility, incident timing and consistency, claimant/account and policy details, necessity or physical damage, and provider/repair documentation, estimates, invoices, and record authenticity. Use independent checks where risk is elevated.
- Missing or incomplete information is not grounds for rejection. Request supporting documents and investigate first; valid claims were wrongly rejected when this was not done (CLM-7003, 7005, 7008, 7021, 7027–7028, 7033). A large paper claim may be valid, and insufficiently reviewed treatment details should not drive rejection.
- Approve when normal checks substantiate the claim and documentation is credible, including small phone/paper claims (CLM-7032, 7035, 7040). Escalate or defer when evidence is insufficient or cannot be independently validated.
- Reject only when fraud, ineligibility, or material contradictions are established. Use verification-first, risk-based decisions rather than categorical rules.

Working notes:

- Size, category, and channel are not conclusive alone. Large online claims can be valid (CLM-7041, 7043), as can small phone, paper, and other claims (CLM-7042, 7044, 7046, 7049–7050). Never approve or reject solely based on amount or submission channel.
- Small online claims remain a high-risk pattern. Fraud was confirmed in CLM-7045, 7047, and 7048, as well as many earlier cases. Require enhanced, independent validation before payment, especially for online auto claims; do not reject solely because the claim is small or online.
- For every claim, verify coverage and eligibility, incident timing and consistency, claimant/account and policy details, treatment necessity or physical damage, and authentic provider, repair, estimate, invoice, photo, and other records. For auto damage, independently confirm the incident, damage pattern, repair estimate, and claimed components.
- Missing or incomplete information is not grounds for immediate rejection. Request supporting documents and investigate first; earlier valid claims were wrongly rejected when this was not done (CLM-7003, 7005, 7008, 7021, 7027–7028, 7033).
- Approve when normal or enhanced checks substantiate the claim and documentation is credible, including small phone/paper claims. Escalate or defer when evidence is insufficient or cannot be independently validated.
- Reject only when fraud, ineligibility, or material contradictions are established. Use verification-first, risk-based decisions rather than categorical rules.

Working notes:

- Size, category, and channel are not conclusive. Large paper/home (CLM-7051, 7059), large online/health (7055), and small phone/auto (7053, 7058, 7060) can be valid; small online claims can be fraudulent (7045, 7047–7048, 7054, 7057). Never approve or reject solely by amount, category, or channel.
- Treat small online auto and health claims as higher-risk patterns requiring enhanced, independent validation, but do not categorically reject them. CLM-7057 shows that approval after merely holding for documents can still allow fraud.
- Before payment, verify coverage and eligibility, incident timing and consistency, claimant/account and policy details, treatment necessity or physical damage, and authentic provider, repair, estimate, invoice, photo, and other records. For auto claims, independently confirm the incident, damage pattern, claimed components, and repair documentation; obtain invoices where appropriate.
- Missing or incomplete information is not immediate grounds for rejection. Request documents and investigate first; valid claims were wrongly rejected when this was skipped (7003, 7005, 7008, 7021, 7027–7028, 7033, 7051, 7053, 7055).
- Approve when normal or enhanced checks substantiate the claim and records are credible, including small phone/paper claims (7052, 7056, 7058–7060). Defer or escalate when evidence is insufficient or cannot yet be independently validated.
- Reject only when fraud, ineligibility, or material contradictions are established. Verification-first, risk-based decisions are preferable to categorical rules.
